t:
In this Act:

    (1) Monument.—The term “Monument” means the Hagerman Fossil Beds National Monument, Idaho, depicted on the National Park Service map numbered 300/80,000, C.O. No. 161, and dated January 7, 1998. 
    (2) Ranch.—The term “Ranch” means the land comprising approximately 1,240 acres situated outside the boundary of the Reserve, known as the “Castle Rock Ranch”. 
    (3) Reserve.—The term “Reserve” means the City of Rocks National Reserve, located near Almo, Idaho, depicted on the National Park Service map numbered 003/80,018, C.O. No. 169, and dated March 25, 1999. 
    (4) Secretary.—The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

fable.w: This section only defines terms (Monument, Ranch, Reserve, Secretary) for the Act. It establishes no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. The reference to places and maps might seem to relate to local interests, but no participation process is created.
fable.s: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior.

opus.w: This section only defines the terms "Monument," "Ranch," "Reserve," and "Secretary." It requires no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. The mention of a "City" and a privately named ranch is just part of place names, not an outside party taking part in a federal decision.
opus.b: Step 1: This section only gives definitions. Words like "City of Rocks National Reserve" and "Castle Rock Ranch" might tempt someone to think a city or private landowner is involved. But the section creates no process, consultation, hearing, or committee with anyone outside the federal government. It names places and defines "the Secretary," and that is all.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used in the Act (Monument, Ranch, Reserve, Secretary). It does not establish any advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with outside entities, or rights to sue. It is purely administrative and definitional.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that defining terms like "Monument" or "Ranch" implies a process of consultation to determine boundaries, but the text itself is purely definitional and contains no procedural requirements for outside involvement.
